draft.title: Token extension grammar (how to mint a new token correctly)
draft.principle_summary: Design-token systems separate a primitive/semantic/component tier structure (CONV, formalized as an exchange format by W3C DTCG but not as a derivation strategy) from the actual math used to place a new value inside an existing ramp. Color extension is solved by JOB-PLACEMENT on a perceptually uniform ramp (Radix's 12-step map, generated in OKLCH for equal perceived contrast per hue per Ottosson 2020), never by picking a hex that looks right. Spacing and radius extension are solved the same way: a small closed set of named roles (not a dense arithmetic ladder) with a geometric, not linear, step relationship, because a linear scale forces near-indistinguishable choices (Eightshapes / Mantlr spacing-system convention). Radius specifically follows a role-tiered scale (Material 3's shape scale is the best-documented public instance) where each step is assigned to a class of component, not derived by formula from the previous step.

sources.claim: OKLCH gives near-uniform perceptual lightness across hues, which is what makes a hue-independent step map (Radix's 12 steps) hold constant contrast; HSL cannot do this because HSL lightness is an RGB math artifact
sources.source: Bjorn Ottosson, OKLab/OKLCH color space (2020); already cited at RATIONALE.md:81

sources.claim: The primitive/semantic/component three-tier token architecture is industry convention; the W3C Design Tokens Community Group's 2025.10 spec standardizes the JSON exchange FORMAT for tokens, explicitly not a derivation strategy
sources.source: designtokens.org, Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10 (W3C Community Group, stable Oct 2025)

sources.claim: Radix's 12-step ramp assigns each step a JOB (backgrounds, component states, borders, solids, text) so the same step number is interchangeable across hues; this is the best-documented public version of that grammar, not an empirical result
sources.source: Radix Colors documentation (radix-ui.com/colors); already cited at RATIONALE.md:731

sources.claim: Spacing scales should be a geometric or otherwise non-linear progression, not linear, because a linear scale offers too many near-identical choices; a common public ladder is 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96
sources.source: Eightshapes, "Space in Design Systems" (Nathan Curtis); Mantlr, "Spacing System Cheat Sheet: 4px vs 8px vs Custom"

sources.claim: Material Design 3's shape (corner-radius) scale assigns named role tiers (none / extra-small 4dp / small 8dp / medium 12dp / large 16dp / extra-large 28dp / full) to classes of component rather than deriving each step from a formula

8pt/4pt base-unit grids are near-universal across major systems (Material, Atlassian) because 8 divides common screen widths (320/768/1024) cleanly, easing responsive scaling; this is a convenience convention, not an empirical finding about usability
sources.source: Material Design spacing methodology; general 8pt-grid design-system literature (freecodecamp.org, prototypr.io)

sources.claim: WCAG contrast math is the correct check to run on any newly-derived color token at its text-role step (Radix step 11-12) against both white and the sunken background
sources.source: WCAG 2.x contrast requirements (already the standing Solen mechanic, cross-domain)

draft.solen_current: RATIONALE.md domain 19 (color-token architecture, lines 727-733) already closes the loop for NEUTRALS ONLY: it names the three-tier primitive/semantic/component split as CONV/W3C-formalized, cites Radix's 12-step job map as the ramp grammar, and gives Solen's actual neutral placements (white=1, sunken #F4F4F5=2-3, border #E4E4E7=6, disabled/ink-3=8-9, ink-2 #6B6B6B=11, ink #0A0A0A=12) with the instruction \"place by JOB on this map instead of inventing a hex.\" The closed semantic-hue table (success/error/warning/star/etc, RATIONALE.md:311-315) is separately locked and explicitly forbids new hues without owner sign-off. Spacing is locked as a 3-tier named rhythm, not a ladder: Section 32px / Card 12px / Group 16px (LOCKFILE.md:442-453, \"three numbers, sitewide\"), with a stated drift signal against any mt-5/mt-6/mt-7 in-between value. Radius is a flat lookup table by component role (card 16, card-lg 20, panel 16, search 99, pill 9999, btn 99, input 12, sheet 28, rounded-2xl 16, rounded-3xl 24, LOCKFILE.md:412-427) plus a nested-radius FORMULA for one specific relationship (inner = outer minus gap, LOCKFILE.md:428-433). The gap register already flags this precisely: G8 at RATIONALE.md:833 reads \"Token extension grammar: neutrals now closed by domain 19's job map; semantic/status extension still CONV.\"
draft.gap: Domain 19 gives a derivation procedure for exactly one case (a new NEUTRAL color) and stops there. Three things are missing and currently have no generative prior: (1) how to derive a genuinely NEW semantic color once an owner has approved a new meaning, since the closed table (line 311) says the set is closed but never says what to do the day it legitimately opens; (2) how to decide whether a spacing need is really one of the existing three tiers misapplied versus a genuine fourth tier, and if the latter, what value to pick, since the locked rhythm names only 32/12/16 with no stated ladder to extend from; (3) how to place a genuinely new radius, since the existing table is an unexplained flat list of ad hoc values (16, 20, 16, 99, 9999, 99, 12, 28, 16, 24) with no shared logic connecting them, so a new one has nothing to be placed relative to except by eyeballing the nearest existing number. Without this, every future one-off token (a loyalty-tier accent, a denser card radius, a fourth spacing step for a genuinely new layout relationship) gets invented from memory exactly the way rule 1 (dont-invent) forbids, and the drift gate has no ladder to check a new literal against.
draft.proposed_addition:
GENERATIVE PRIOR, Token extension grammar (extends domain 19 from neutrals-only to all three token kinds).

Before minting ANYTHING, classify the need: is this a new JOB inside an existing ramp/table (extend), or a new MEANING/RELATIONSHIP that has no place in the existing set at all (open)? Extend is the default path; open requires an explicit owner decision logged in TASTE_LOG before any value is picked, per the closed-table rule at RATIONALE.md:311. This prior only covers HOW to derive the value once extend is confirmed or open is owner-approved; it never re-opens a frozen literal.

COLOR:
1. If the need is a new step within an existing hue (e.g. one more neutral, a hover-state border): place it by JOB on the Radix 12-step map exactly as domain 19 already prescribes for neutrals (steps 1-2 app bg, 3-5 component bg, 6-8 borders, 9-10 solids, 11-12 text), generating the missing value between its two ramp neighbors in OKLCH (not HSL, not a guessed hex) so perceived lightness stays evenly spaced.
2. If the need is a genuinely new semantic hue (owner-approved addition to the closed table): derive in OKLCH, holding lightness in the same visible weight-class as the other saturated semantic tokens already in the table (success #16A34A, error #D32F2F, star #FFC32B etc, compared by eye against the existing swatch strip, not by asserting an unverified hex-to-OKLCH conversion here) so the new color reads neither louder nor quieter than its siblings; pick a hue angle that stays clear of the red/green confusable pair on the CVD axis (domain 3, T1) if any other status color is already adjacent. Convert to hex, then verify WCAG contrast at the text-role step (11-12) against both white and s-bg-sunken before shipping.
3. Name every new token by MEANING (s-<meaning>), never by hue or vendor name. Log the addition and the owner's yes in TASTE_LOG in the same turn.

SPACING:
Solen's 32/12/16 rhythm is a deliberately small NAMED set, not a truncated ladder, so the first move on "I need a new gap" is to re-check whether the need is actually Section, Card, or Group misapplied, not a fourth tier. Only mint a new tier if the relationship being spaced is categorically different from page-section, sibling-card, and in-card-group (all three already covered). If so, derive the value from the standard geometric spacing convention (CONV, not empirical, per Eightshapes/Mantlr): 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, doubling or near-doubling rather than incrementing by a fixed step, because a linear +4px ladder produces choices too close to discriminate by eye. Pick the nearest rung that is also a genuine 4pt multiple, and name the new token by RELATIONSHIP (what sits next to what), mirroring Section/Card/Group, never by raw pixel value alone, so the existing drift signal (flagging bare mt-5/mt-6/mt-7 literals) keeps working against it.

RADIUS:
Retroactively, Solen's existing flat table maps almost exactly onto Material 3's public shape-scale role tiers (CONV: none / extra-small 4 / small 8 / medium 12 / large 16 / extra-large 28 / full): input 12 sits at "medium" (form fields), card/card-lg/panel/rounded-2xl at 16-20 sit at "large" (cards, dialogs), sheet 28 sits at "extra-large" (expanded sheets), pill/btn/search/rounded-full at 99-9999 sit at "full" (pills, circular controls). That correspondence is the evidence a new radius should also land on one of these role bands, not a freehand number: identify which role class the new element belongs to (field-level control, card/container, expanded sheet/modal, or fully-round chip), take the Solen value already assigned to a sibling in that class, and reuse it rather than deriving a new number. If the element genuinely sits inside an existing rounded container, apply the already-locked nested-radius formula (inner = outer minus gap, LOCKFILE.md:428-433) to confirm the borrowed value does not visually bulge against its parent; if the formula's result is closer to another existing role value than to the borrowed one, use the formula's result instead of inventing a new literal.

BOUNDARY: this prior never authorizes reopening the closed semantic-hue table, the 32/12/16 rhythm, or any single frozen radius literal in LOCKFILE.md; it only supplies the derivation math for the day an owner-approved new need shows up, so that day does not default to a hand-picked hex or pixel value.
draft.taste_lab_probe: Pick 2-3 extension candidates that are plausible in the near-term build queue (for example: a loyalty-tier accent distinct from the existing status set, a denser radius for a compact list-row card if one gets built, or a spacing relationship for a layout that is neither page-section, sibling-card, nor in-card-group). For each candidate, generate ONE value via the procedure above (job-placed on the relevant ramp/table) and ONE value picked freehand by eye on the same real Solen surface, rendered side by side in situ (never as an isolated swatch). Ask the owner a forced binary choice without telling them which is which: does one look wrong, or are they indistinguishable. Indistinguishable or a preference for the derived value is a pass signal for trusting the procedure on future one-offs without a mockup round; a clear preference for the freehand pick means the procedure's placement logic needs a documented exception for that token kind before it is relied on again. No target pass rate is asserted since no prior study of this exact procedure exists; the probe's job is qualitative calibration, not a statistic.

claim_verdicts.claim: OKLab/OKLCH (Ottosson 2020) gives near-uniform perceptual lightness across hues; HSL cannot because HSL-L is an RGB math artifact
claim_verdicts.note: Correct and well-established. Also independently confirmed already cited verbatim at RATIONALE.md:81 in this repo.

claim_verdicts.claim: W3C Design Tokens Community Group's 2025.10 spec standardizes the JSON exchange format for tokens, not a derivation strategy
claim_verdicts.note: Verified live: designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/format/ and the W3C community group announcement (28 Oct 2025) confirm this is the first stable version and is a format spec, not a derivation methodology. Matches RATIONALE.md:729 wording exactly.

claim_verdicts.claim: Radix's 12-step ramp assigns each step a job (backgrounds, component states, borders, solids, text) so the same step number is interchangeable across hues
claim_verdicts.note: Verified against radix-ui.com/colors documentation: steps 1-2 backgrounds, 3-5 component bg (normal/hover/pressed), 6-8 borders, 9-10 solids, 11-12 text. Matches almost verbatim. Already cited at RATIONALE.md:731.

claim_verdicts.claim: Spacing scales should be geometric/non-linear (not linear) because linear offers too many near-identical choices; a common ladder is 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96
claim_verdicts.note: Mantlr's actual article (verified live) argues for an 8px base with a 4px sub-grid and a general 4pt/8pt convention, but does NOT explicitly publish the specific 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96 ladder as printed in the draft - that specific numeric ladder is the researcher's own construction from the general 4pt-multiple convention, not a verbatim citation from either named source. Tier CONV is still honest (this is convention-level, not empirical), but the verified_addition should not imply the exact ladder was lifted from Mantlr verbatim.

claim_verdicts.claim: Material Design 3's shape scale assigns named role tiers (none/extra-small 4dp/small 8dp/medium 12dp/large 16dp/extra-large 28dp/full) to component classes rather than deriving each step by formula
claim_verdicts.note: Verified live against m3.material.io/styles/shape/corner-radius-scale: extra-large is confirmed 28dp on that exact page (a differently-scoped Jetpack Compose token set uses 24dp for a similar-but-not-identical tier, which is a platform-implementation variant, not a contradiction of the cited primary source).

claim_verdicts.claim: 8pt/4pt base-unit grids are near-universal because 8 divides common screen widths cleanly, and this is a convenience convention not an empirical usability finding
claim_verdicts.note: Standard, uncontested framing, correctly tiered as CONV rather than T1.

claim_verdicts.claim: WCAG contrast math is the correct check for a newly-derived color token at its text-role step against white and the sunken background
claim_verdicts.note: Standard, uncontested, already the standing Solen mechanic per the draft's own note.

<residual_risks>Two soft points, neither a myth-screen hit and neither load-bearing enough to flag the whole stream: (1) the specific spacing ladder "4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96" printed in the research draft is not a verbatim quote from either cited source (Eightshapes or Mantlr); Mantlr's live article argues the general 4pt-multiple/geometric-doubling convention but does not publish that exact 9-value list. Softened in verified_addition to describe the convention rather than assert the specific list was lifted from a source. (2) Material 3's shape scale has a platform-variant discrepancy: the primary cited page (m3.material.io/styles/shape/corner-radius-scale) confirms extra-large = 28dp as the draft states, but Jetpack Compose's M3 token implementation uses 24dp for its "extraLarge" token, a real platform-specific divergence from the design spec, not a research error. Not a lock tension for Solen (Solen's own sheet radius is 28, matching the design-spec page, not Compose), but worth a QUESTIONS.md note if anyone later cites "Material 3 extra-large" from a different (Compose-sourced) context and gets 24 instead of 28.</residual_risks>
